key_insight: Diagnosis-specific language-model adaptation plus multi-expert weighting improved 180-day opioid overdose risk prediction from prior-year ICD histories.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help flag patients at elevated overdose risk earlier and more accurately than general-purpose models, supporting better prioritization of preventive outreach.
method: Continued pretraining on longitudinal ICD diagnosis sequences.
Fine-tuned two adapted models: OODMAMBA and OODQWEN.
Built OVERDOSEMOE to combine multiple model scales with complementary expert-weighting strategies.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, OODQWEN reached AUPRC 24.47 and AUROC 68.56, while OVERDOSEMOE improved to AUPRC 25.17 and AUROC 69.49 and was also tested on an independent MIMIC-IV cohort.
watch_item: Performance gains are promising, but real-world deployment would need careful validation for calibration, generalizability, and safe use across different EHR settings and patient populations.
paper_title: OverdoseMoE: A Multi-Expert Framework for Opioid Overdose Risk Prediction
